tools.name: portfolixir.transactions.list
tools.title: List transactions
tools.description: List transactions. Filters: from/to (ISO dates), portfolio_id, security_id, securities_account_id. Optional fields: a sparse fieldset, prefer a small one. Every read echoes limit (default 10000, at most 50000) and truncated. Optional since (FR-38, ISO8601 UTC) is a delta read: rows created or updated strictly after it, oldest change first, with as_of (this read's next since; on has_more=true a cursor at the page's last row, or, with no ~id, poll later: a write is in flight) and a delta_note; with since, page by as_of, never offset. A later read may re-deliver a row, never skip one; deletions are not shown. Optional running_balance_for (a cash account id) adds each row's running_balance, that account's balance after it in its currency, folded over its whole history (true on a narrowed read; null on a row not moving it), and a running_balance_basis.

from.description: An ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) from 1900-01-01 to 2999-12-31, else a 422 naming the field with nothing stored.

to.description: An ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) from 1900-01-01 to 2999-12-31, else a 422 naming the field with nothing stored.

tools.name: portfolixir.transactions.create
tools.title: Create transaction
tools.description: Create a transaction of any bookable kind: buy, sell, dividend, interest, deposit, removal, fee, tax, tax_refund, cash_transfer, inbound_delivery, outbound_delivery, security_transfer (balance anchors: set_balance). Required fields by kind: buy/sell need securities_account_id, security_id, quantity and price; dividend needs security_id, cash_account_id and gross_amount; interest/deposit/removal/fee/tax/tax_refund need cash_account_id and gross_amount; cash_transfer needs cash_account_id, counter_cash_account_id and gross_amount; deliveries need securities_account_id, security_id and quantity — inbound_delivery additionally REQUIRES price (an unpriced inbound delivery enters the cost basis at zero), while outbound_delivery removes cost at the running average, price informational; security_transfer needs securities_account_id, counter_securities_account_id, security_id and quantity. An interest booking may name the security whose coupon it is. For buy/sell, omit cash_account_id (the depot's linked account). Amounts are positive magnitudes; the kind implies the direction (removal/fee/tax debit, deposit/dividend/interest/tax_refund credit) — never send negative values: a refunded tax (after a loss sale) is its own tax_refund with a positive gross_amount, not a negative taxes field (only set_balance takes a negative). Semantics: for dividend/interest/tax_refund, gross_amount is the NET cash credited — withheld taxes go in taxes; the income report adds them back. A security settled through a cash account in another currency is booked in the security currency with security_amount (trade amount in it), settlement_amount (trade amount in the account currency, before fees and taxes) and settlement_fx_rate (account units per security unit; derived from the two amounts when omitted), Decimal strings. currency_code: the security's or the account's, else 422. The cash and the settlement must agree (#395): a cross-currency buy's gross_amount (cash paid, costs included) must equal settlement_amount + fees + taxes, a sell's settlement_amount - fees - taxes, within 0.01, else a 422 on gross_amount names the implied amount. Always send gross_amount on a cross-currency trade: without it the ledger books quantity × price plus fees and taxes (less on a sell) as the account's cash, checked the same way; a trade with a rate but neither gross_amount nor settlement_amount answers 422 on gross_amount. Amounts are rounded half up to 6 decimal places (a quantity to 12) before they are checked, so the stored, answered and journaled value is the rounded one, and a positive amount that rounds to 0 answers 422; an amount with more than 14 digits before the decimal point (a quantity more than 18) answers 422 naming the field. A timeout or lost connection answers outcome unknown (ApiOutcomeUnknownError): the write may have committed, so re-read before retrying; a blind retry can store a duplicate.

date.description: An ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) from 1900-01-01 to 2999-12-31, else a 422 naming the field with nothing stored.

tools.name: portfolixir.transactions.update
tools.title: Update transaction
tools.description: Patch a transaction. As on create: a dividend's gross_amount is the NET cash credited (withheld taxes go in taxes), and an unpriced inbound delivery enters the cost basis at zero. A patch that changes gross_amount, settlement_amount, fees, taxes, type, currency_code, security_id, cash_account_id or securities_account_id — or, on a booking without gross_amount, quantity or price — re-checks the cross-currency settlement agreement (#395) and the trade's currency; a patch of notes or date on an older booking is never refused by them. A stored split row changes only its notes (else 422); a wrong split: portfolixir.splits.delete, then rebook. On a trade storing gross_amount, no settlement_amount, a patch of quantity, price, fees, taxes or buy/sell type must state gross_amount, agreeing with quantity × price ± fees/taxes within 0.01 + an unchanged price's rounding (else 422). A patch that loses a race to a concurrent write answers 409 with errors.detail alone and saves nothing: re-read it and retry. Amounts are rounded half up to 6 decimal places (a quantity to 12) before they are checked, so the stored, answered and journaled value is the rounded one, and a positive amount that rounds to 0 answers 422; an amount with more than 14 digits before the decimal point (a quantity more than 18) answers 422 naming the field.

date.description: An ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) from 1900-01-01 to 2999-12-31, else a 422 naming the field with nothing stored.

tools.name: portfolixir.transactions.delete
tools.title: Delete transaction
tools.description: Delete a transaction; a split: portfolixir.splits.delete.

tools.name: portfolixir.transactions.rate_only
tools.title: Rate-only trades (data quality)
tools.description: Cross-currency trades with a settlement_fx_rate and no gross_amount or settlement_amount, any gap: figures, booked_cash, expected_cash (at its rate), difference; as_of, note, remedy. Fix: the broker's cash as gross_amount via transactions.update.

tools.name: portfolixir.transactions.cash_mismatch
tools.title: Cash mismatches (data quality)
tools.description: Trades storing gross_amount, no settlement_amount, whose cash misses quantity × price ± fees/taxes beyond tolerance (0.01 + the price's rounding): stored_cash, derived_cash, difference, tolerance; as_of, note, remedy. Fix: gross_amount via transactions.update.

tools.name: portfolixir.splits.preview
tools.title: Preview stock split
tools.description: Preview of a stock split (ADR-0028), nothing written: per portfolio holding the security, the quantity just before and after the effective date and the resulting current position, plus warnings (Decimal strings). ALWAYS call it before portfolixir.splits.create. effective_date_before_history: the date predates the security's first transaction, so stored quantities may already be post-split (Portfolio Performance's split wizard rewrites history) and booking would double-adjust; do not book when before/after are 0 and the current position already looks post-split. quotes_around shows the stored closes around the date and quote_basis_check compares the jump with each row's basis: quote_basis_contradiction means the series contradicts its source classification — resolve it (for a never-adjusting provider set the security's treat_quotes_as_raw via portfolixir.securities.update) instead of booking blindly; insufficient_quotes_to_verify_basis: too few closes to check. A row's bookable flag is false when the portfolio held nothing on the date, so booking creates no row for it; with no bookable row the preview warns no_position_at_effective_date and splits.create fails. The ratio is two positive integers (10:1 forward, 1:10 reverse), normalized to lowest terms; the security's splits, each by its own magnitude (2:1 and 1:2 both count 2), may multiply to at most 10^12 with this one, else 422 on ratio.

date.description: Effective date, not in the future. An ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) from 1900-01-01 to 2999-12-31, else a 422 naming the field with nothing stored.

ratio_numerator.description: New shares per ratio_denominator old ones (10 for 10:1, 1 for 1:10).

tools.name: portfolixir.splits.create
tools.title: Book stock split
tools.description: Book a stock split as a ledger event (ADR-0028): ONE call fans it out across all portfolios holding a position in the security at the effective date, one journaled split row per portfolio, inserted atomically; do not call once per portfolio. A second same-day split for the same security is rejected naming the existing event (a retried timeout cannot compound it), so a 422 naming an existing transaction means it is already booked; a wrong one is removed with portfolixir.splits.delete. A future effective date, and a security nobody held on it, are rejected. Check portfolixir.splits.preview first, above all its effective_date_before_history warning. Ratio parts are positive integers (never Decimal strings); past a combined 10^12 of the security's splits, each by its own magnitude, it answers 422 on ratio and writes nothing. Answers the created transactions, financial values as strings. A timeout or lost connection answers outcome unknown (ApiOutcomeUnknownError): the write may have committed, so re-read before retrying; a blind retry can store a duplicate.

date.description: Effective date, not in the future. An ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) from 1900-01-01 to 2999-12-31, else a 422 naming the field with nothing stored.

ratio_numerator.description: New shares per ratio_denominator old ones (10 for 10:1, 1 for 1:10).

tools.name: portfolixir.splits.delete
tools.title: Delete stock split
tools.description: Delete a booked split whole (ADR-0028) from any of its rows: every portfolio's row of the event goes in one step, each journaled, and a corrected ratio can then be booked with portfolixir.splits.create; portfolixir.transactions.delete removes one row only and leaves the event. Answers the removed rows, Decimal strings; 404 if the row is gone, 422 if it is no split.

tools.name: portfolixir.splits.incomplete
tools.title: Incomplete splits (data quality)
tools.description: Split events missing a portfolio that held the security entering the date (lots scaled, holding not): security, date, ratio, booked_portfolio_ids, transaction_ids, missing_portfolios with quantity_before; as_of, note, remedy. Fix: rebook via portfolixir.splits.create (adds only the missing rows), or splits.delete.

tools.name: portfolixir.holdings.list
tools.title: List holdings
tools.description: Per-portfolio derived holdings with moving-average cost basis, latest price (quote, else last own trade; price_source), market value and unrealized P&L in each security's OWN currency, plus the ADR-0033 base-currency P&L decomposition per row: base_cost (the settlement leg, in base_currency), price_return_* (the security's own price move at today's rate), currency_return_* (the FX effect on the invested amount) and total_return_base_* — total = price + currency exactly; cost_basis and base_cost leave out the buys' fees and taxes (computation_basis). decomposed false with undecomposed_reason (missing_native_cost | missing_base_cost | missing_fx | no_price) marks a row whose figure is honestly unavailable, never guessed; currency_basis_note states each field's currency. Decimal strings. Rows carry isin and wkn (null if absent): broker reconciliation needs no securities.list join. Base-currency totals and cash quote: portfolixir.portfolios.valuation; a per-security EUR view across portfolios: portfolixir.holdings.by_security. Optional filters: security_id, securities_account_id. Optional fields selects a sparse fieldset: each row then carries exactly those fields — prefer a small one (e.g. security_id, quantity, market_value).

tools.name: portfolixir.cashflow.realized_gains
tools.title: Realized gains roll-up
tools.description: FIFO realized P&L across ALL securities and portfolios (the Trades facet), by close date into a year -> month matrix. FX: a sale converts at the EUR hub rate of ITS OWN close date, or, closing a lot booked in another currency, reads the base cash its bookings moved (realized_base_source); one with no rate that day or an unavailable_reason is in no total, named in excluded (by_reason: no_rate, missing_settlement_leg, third_currency, other_account_currency, zero_amount). Decimal strings; computation_basis states every rule. Optional limit keeps the newest matrix years, echoed with truncated. `trades`: round-trips, newest close first: security, open/close dates, holding_period_days, quantity, basis, proceeds, realized_pnl_abs/_pct in the trade currency, realized_base in the base, and annualized_return (XIRR p.a., trade currency), null with annualized_return_reason on a zero basis (realized_pnl_pct null too), under 365 days held or when no rate solves. `summary`: realized_total, hit_rate (results > 0) and average_holding_period_days over the matrix's trades; null, not 0, with none. `unmatched_sells`: count and each sell's security, date and quantity no buy was matched to (an inbound delivery opens no lot); in no figure.

limit.description: newest years of the annual matrix to keep (default 100, at most 1000)

tools.name: portfolixir.cashflow.external_flows
tools.title: Deposits & withdrawals roll-up
tools.description: The Cash-flow Deposits-&-withdrawals facet's roll-up (issue #725): the booked external CASH flows — deposit and removal transactions — across all portfolios, grouped by booking date into a year -> month matrix with deposits, withdrawals and a net per year. Deliberately narrower than the performance walk's invested_capital, which additionally counts securities delivered in/out at market value and balance-snapshot residuals; that difference is stated in computation_basis.excludes so the two figures can differ without either lying. FX basis: each flow converts via the EUR hub at the rate stored on ITS OWN booking date; a flow with no stored rate for that day is excluded from every total and named by its cash account in `excluded`. Financial values are Decimal strings. Optional limit keeps the newest years of the matrix, echoed with truncated; computation_basis.window names the cut.

limit.description: newest years of the annual matrix to keep (default 100, at most 1000)

tools.name: portfolixir.cashflow.costs
tools.title: Fees & taxes roll-up
tools.description: The Cash-flow Costs facet's roll-up: what the portfolio cost to run, at OVERVIEW level only — fees and taxes across all portfolios, grouped by booking date into a year/month matrix of fees, taxes and a total per month and per year (computation_basis.totals). The series sums the fee and tax LEGS riding any transaction plus the standalone fee/tax bookings, with tax_refund netted against taxes; gross amounts are never summed (a buy's gross includes its legs while a sell's is net of them — summing gross would describe something else). FX basis: each cost converts via the EUR hub at the rate stored on ITS OWN booking date; a cost with no stored rate for that day is excluded from every total and named by its currency in `excluded`. Decimal strings. Optional limit keeps the newest years of the matrix, echoed with truncated; computation_basis.window names the cut.

limit.description: newest years of the annual matrix to keep (default 100, at most 1000)

tools.name: portfolixir.holdings.by_security
tools.title: Holdings by security (global EUR)
tools.description: Global per-security valuation across ALL portfolios: each held security's total quantity and current market value converted to the EUR hub, with a valued flag (false when a quote, trade price or EUR rate path is missing) and an unvalued_reason (no_price: nothing resolves at all; missing_fx: latest_price/price_currency are known but no stored rate path reaches EUR; null when valued). Each row also carries latest_price, price_currency, price_source and price_date (when that price is from). Self-describing: currency EUR, an as_of read date and a note; financial values are Decimal strings. Differs from portfolixir.holdings.list (per-portfolio holdings in the security's own currency, no FX) and from portfolixir.portfolios.valuation (one portfolio's totals/weights in its base currency).

tools.name: portfolixir.holdings.negative
tools.title: Negative holdings (data quality)
tools.description: (depot, security) positions below zero (debris of unmodeled corporate actions), with names and each security's total across ALL depots (transfer debris vs. a truly negative total); as_of, note. Repair via portfolixir.transactions.*; nothing changes automatically.

tools.name: portfolixir.holdings.reconcile
tools.title: Reconcile external position list (read-only)
tools.description: Compare an external position list (broker statement, depot overview) with the ledger-derived holdings; read-only, nothing stored. Each row's identifier is matched through the stable-identity ladder (ISIN incl. recorded former ISINs, then WKN / ticker+currency / name+currency with an exactly-one rule across those tiers); the response reports per matched security the matched_via tier, the exact ledger quantity, external quantity and delta as Decimal strings, plus ambiguous rows with candidates, unmatched rows, and held ledger positions absent from the list. Rows of one security are aggregated: one delta per position. Resolve a difference by booking the missing transaction of the correct kind (buy, sell, delivery with price, transfer, dividend, tax_refund for a tax credited back after a loss sale, ...) via portfolixir.transactions.create — balance snapshots (set_balance) and unpriced deliveries are last resorts that distort cost basis; do NOT reach for them just to make numbers match. Weak (ticker/name) matches carry a caveat: confirm the security before booking anything. Quantities: canonical dot-decimal strings; parse locale formats client-side. Optional scope: portfolio_id or view (mutually exclusive); default is the whole instance, and the response states its basis (as_of, scope).

rows.description: The external position list, one row per line of the source document. At most 10000 rows per request.

identifier.description: The row's security identifier as the external document shows it: an ISIN, WKN, ticker or name. ISIN-shaped strings match via the ISIN tier only (recorded former ISINs included).

quantity.description: External quantity as a canonical dot-decimal string (e.g. "12.5").

currency.description: The row's currency (e.g. EUR). Required for ticker/name matching — a currency-less row can only match by ISIN or WKN and is otherwise unmatched.

security_id.description: Optional pin: match this row to the given security, bypassing the ladder.

portfolio_id.description: Optional scope: compare against this portfolio's ledger quantities only.

view.description: Optional scope: compare against the holdings matching this bucket view. Mutually exclusive with portfolio_id.

tools.name: portfolixir.portfolios.valuation
tools.title: Value portfolio
tools.description: Live valuation of a portfolio: market values, actual weights per position, plus the base-currency portfolio total, cash balances and the cash quote (use this, not holdings.list, for base-currency totals). The valued/price_source flags mark stale or unpriceable positions, each position's price_date says when its price is from, stale_priced_count counts the quoted positions whose quote is older than the data-quality threshold, retired holdings left out (the operator's remedy is the security's is_retired flag, which the performance walk keys on, or a quote sync), newest_quote_date is the newest stored quote date across the quoted, non-retired positions (null when none is quote-priced), and unvalued_reason distinguishes no_price (nothing resolves) from missing_fx (a native latest_price/price_currency is known but no stored FX path reaches the base currency). An optional view (a view id) scopes the result to that bucket view's holdings and is echoed. Pass include_positions=false for a roll-up-only read — totals, cash balances and cash quote without the per-position rows; the response states positions_included. Scope twin: portfolixir.views.valuation — this tool answers ONE portfolio record in its base currency, its view narrowing within that portfolio; the twin answers a view across EVERY portfolio, each account counted once, in EUR or, with no id, the total of every account. For a total, read that, not a sum of portfolios.

tools.name: portfolixir.exchange_rates.list
tools.title: List exchange rates
tools.description: List stored EUR-hub exchange rates, most recent first. limit (default 50000, max 200000) is echoed with truncated.

tools.name: portfolixir.exchange_rates.sync
tools.title: Sync exchange rates
tools.description: Fetch and store exchange rates from the configured provider (ECB, EUR hub). scope=latest (default): today's rates only. scope=history: the one-shot BACKFILL of the whole historical series, so a dated conversion (a realized gain, a cost, an excluded flow) finds a rate; run it when a cashflow facet reports excluded rows. A day the ECB did not publish stays excluded and named. Having stored rates, it derives the missing settlement legs of imported cross-currency trades, journaled. Returns {provider, status, upserted, scope, settlement_legs: {status completed|not_run|stopped, derived, skipped_no_rate, skipped_changed, skipped_zero_amount, stopped_at_transaction_id}}; a stop keeps the rates (re-run); latest derives none (null). No history: 422; provider or store failure: 502, nothing stored; a second backfill while one runs: 409. A timeout or lost connection answers outcome unknown (ApiOutcomeUnknownError): the write may have committed, so re-read before retrying; a blind retry can store a duplicate.

tools.name: portfolixir.classifications.list
tools.title: List classifications
tools.description: List classification trees with categories and assignments.

tools.name: portfolixir.classifications.create
tools.title: Create classification
tools.description: Create a custom classification tree. A timeout or lost connection answers outcome unknown (ApiOutcomeUnknownError): the write may have committed, so re-read before retrying; a blind retry can store a duplicate.

tools.name: portfolixir.classifications.categories.create
tools.title: Create category
tools.description: Create a category in a custom tree. A parent_id must name a category of the same classification, and a tree has at most 32 levels; any other parent answers 422 on parent_id and nothing is written. A timeout or lost connection answers outcome unknown (ApiOutcomeUnknownError): the write may have committed, so re-read before retrying; a blind retry can store a duplicate.

tools.name: portfolixir.classifications.update
tools.title: Update classification
tools.description: Update a custom tree's name, description or position.

tools.name: portfolixir.classifications.delete
tools.title: Delete classification
tools.description: Delete a custom classification (not a built-in). ONE CALL REMOVES, with it: every category of the tree, at every depth; every security's assignment in it; every target weight on its categories; and every target plan of the tree, in every portfolio, view and version, with its cash target. Securities stay. Each row, the assignments too, is journaled as its own delete before the classification's. A tree a policy rule reads is refused with 409 naming the rules. dry_run true deletes nothing: it answers would_remove (count and ids per kind) or the refusal.

tools.name: portfolixir.classifications.categories.update
tools.title: Update category
tools.description: Patch a category. A new parent_id must name a category of the same classification that is neither the category itself nor one of its descendants, and a tree has at most 32 levels; any other parent answers 422 on parent_id and nothing is written.

tools.name: portfolixir.classifications.categories.delete
tools.title: Delete category
tools.description: Delete a custom classification's category. ONE CALL REMOVES, with it: its sub-categories at every depth; the assignments to any of them; and the target weights on any of them, category and position alike, in every plan. Each row is journaled as its own delete, the lowest categories first and itself last. A category a policy rule reads, itself or below it, is refused with 409 naming the rules. dry_run true deletes nothing: it answers would_remove (count and ids per kind) or the refusal.

tools.name: portfolixir.classifications.assign
tools.title: Assign security
tools.description: Assign a security to a category of a custom tree.

tools.name: portfolixir.classifications.assign_bulk
tools.title: Assign securities (bulk)
tools.description: Assign many securities to one category in a single call.

tools.name: portfolixir.classifications.unassign
tools.title: Unassign security
tools.description: Remove a security's assignment from a classification.

tools.name: portfolixir.trades.list
tools.title: List trades
tools.description: FIFO-matched trades: open lots, closed round-trips, orphan sells. A round-trip is in its sell's currency_code, each lot entering through its own settlement legs; if a lot has no leg in it, unavailable_reason is missing_settlement_leg, third_currency (a sell's proceeds null too), other_account_currency or zero_amount; lots_missing_leg names each lot with its reason; cost and result null. A trade's basis includes the buys' fees and taxes, proceeds are net of the sell's; an open lot's prices, base_cost and P&L leave them out; its buy_fees/buy_taxes are the whole buy's, for original_quantity, the share already sold being in the closed trade's. Each: realized P&L, annualized_return (XIRR p.a., trade currency), null with annualized_return_reason (zero basis, under 365 days held, no rate solves); computation_basis states the rules. An open lot: buy_price as recorded, buy_price_native (its P&L's basis, null without it) and, as holdings.list, latest_price (quote, else last own trade price), price_source, price_date and decomposition fields. from/to filter each leg by its date; no limit.

from.description: An ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) from 1900-01-01 to 2999-12-31, else a 422 naming the field with nothing stored.

to.description: An ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) from 1900-01-01 to 2999-12-31, else a 422 naming the field with nothing stored.

tools.name: portfolixir.sales.hindsight
tools.title: What each sale missed
tools.description: FR-50: one row per sale booking (orphan sells included, outbound deliveries not), newest first: the sold security's price return in EUR over 1m, 3m, 12m (calendar months) and latest (its latest close), from the close standing for the sale day (at most 7 days older; the booked price enters no figure) to end_on's. benchmark (rate:<decimal> a year, or security:<id> flagged is_benchmark) adds its return and difference = security - benchmark. status: complete, pending (ends after today) or incomplete with reason no_start_close, no_end_close, no_fx_rate or no_benchmark_close (its figure kept). Price only: a dividend payer's miss is understated. include reinvestment adds what the switch cost, buys FOUND BY RULE, never chosen: buys from the same cash account within 30 days, of another security, take proceeds oldest first (buys, share_of_proceeds_matched, unallocated, days_to_first_buy, or no_match, reason); per span kept (that share of the sold position) and switched (the bought positions, cash until each buy) in EUR, difference = switched + taxes_apart - kept, BEFORE TAX (fees_inside; the sale's taxes_apart added back), PRICE ONLY (income_apart, never added). IT SCORES NOTHING AND GIVES NO VERDICT. portfolio_id, security_id, from/to (sale date) narrow; limit is echoed with truncated. Decimals are strings; computation_basis states the rules.

from.description: An ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) from 1900-01-01 to 2999-12-31, else a 422 naming the field with nothing stored.

to.description: An ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) from 1900-01-01 to 2999-12-31, else a 422 naming the field with nothing stored.

benchmark.description: rate:0.02 = 2 % p.a., or security:<id> flagged is_benchmark

tools.name: portfolixir.targets.list
tools.title: List target weights
tools.description: List a portfolio's stored target weights (SOLL). Optional classification_id scopes to one tree; optional view (a view id) selects its plan; optional plan_id reads that plan version, 422 on plan_id when archived or of another portfolio, classification or view. Optional since (ISO8601 UTC) makes this a delta read: only rows changed strictly after it return, a row changing when it OR its plan does (activating a version re-delivers its rows). The response carries as_of, the next since (a later read may re-deliver a row but never skips one) and a delta_note; deletions are NOT represented: a removed row, or one of a plan no longer active, shows only on a full read.

since.description: ISO8601 instant (UTC) or date; delta read, see the tool description

tools.name: portfolixir.targets.set
tools.title: Set target weights
tools.description: Upsert target weights for one portfolio and classification. Each target_weight is a string fraction in [0,1] with at most 6 decimal places (a finer one answers 422). An entry with only a category_id sets that category's weight; adding a security_id (ADR-0030) sets a position weight on that security, which must sit under the category. Category and position rows coexist; a category's effective target rolls up from its positions. A plan carries at most one position row per security (a second category, a repeat in the batch, or a write losing a race to file it elsewhere answers 422); a batch names each category row once per batch and carries at most one row per category and per security assigned in the classification, never more than 10000, else a 422 names targets and nothing is written. Weight sums are not enforced. Optional plan_id writes that plan version (a draft from portfolixir.plans.duplicate) instead of the view's active plan; an archived plan, or one of another portfolio, classification or view, answers 422 on plan_id.

tools.name: portfolixir.targets.delete
tools.title: Delete target weight
tools.description: Remove a portfolio's target weight for one category. Optional plan_id: as on portfolixir.targets.set.

tools.name: portfolixir.targets.list_positions
tools.title: List position targets
tools.description: List a portfolio's position-level SOLL targets (ADR-0030): a target_weight (string fraction in [0,1]) per individual security under a category, plus each affected category's effective roll-up (explicit weight, position sum, effective weight and a conflict flag on their mismatch). Sums are not enforced, so a category's position sum may differ from its explicit weight or 1. Each position row carries security_id, security_name and a stale flag — true when its security no longer sits under the stored category; the row still counts where it was filed; re-file it (delete_position + set under the current category). The roll-up carries has_stale per category. Optional classification_id scopes to one tree; optional view (a view id) selects its plan; plan_id: as on portfolixir.targets.list; drift_basis names a draft. min_drift (an absolute drift-weight threshold as a Decimal string, e.g. "0.02") returns only the position rows whose |drift_weight| meets it, where drift_weight is the security's actual weight in the steering basis minus its position target, renormalised for a short plan (ADR-0040), as the allocation computes it; kept rows carry drift_weight, rows without a drift are filtered out, and the response states min_drift, position_targets_total (the pre-filter count) and drift_basis. Without min_drift the rows carry no drift_weight. Optional since (ISO8601 UTC) makes the position rows a delta read as on portfolixir.targets.list (a later read may re-deliver a row, never skip one), applied before min_drift, so position_targets_total counts the delta; effective_targets always covers the whole plan.

min_drift.description: absolute drift-weight threshold as a finite, non-negative Decimal string, e.g. "0.02"; NaN or Infinity answers 422

since.description: ISO8601 instant (UTC) or date; delta read, see the tool description

tools.name: portfolixir.targets.delete_position
tools.title: Delete position target
tools.description: Remove a portfolio's position-level SOLL target for one security under a category (ADR-0030). The category target and the category's other positions are left in place. Optional plan_id: as on portfolixir.targets.set.

tools.name: portfolixir.portfolios.allocation
tools.title: Portfolio allocation drift
tools.description: SOLL/IST allocation breakdown for a portfolio against one classification: market value, actual weight, target weight and drift per category plus a cash row. Drift is actual - target (positive = overweight; ADR-0023), as a weight and restated in base currency. A plan may deliberately allocate less than 100% (ADR-0040): unallocated_remainder states that gap as part of the plan, and drift_basis names what drift was measured against: "allocated_portion" (each target renormalised to the allocated share, so the remainder is no phantom overweight) or "full_plan" (the plan sums to 100%). Category targets are the EFFECTIVE targets (ADR-0030): when the plan carries position-level SOLL rows their sum steers the category — conflict flags a diverging explicit category weight, has_stale a stale position row. Each category's positions are the union of its held positions and the plan's position SOLL rows: each row carries quantity, target_weight (its position SOLL, null when none), drift_weight (actual - target), held, drift_value and rebalance_quantity (indicative units to sell (positive) or buy (negative)) — display-only hints, never an order. A position with SOLL > 0 that is not yet held appears with IST 0 (held=false) and its hint priced at the latest stored quote (null without a price); quote_date names that quote's date (null when the hint is not quote-based), and held means holdings presence — an unpriceable held security is never reported as unheld. A row is hidden only when its SOLL is 0/absent and holdings are zero; stale=true marks a row whose SOLL row no longer matches the security's current category (it keeps counting where it was filed). Unassigned entries attach their position SOLL too, and deep_target_sum reports the effective targets steered below an untargeted top level. Rows without their own SOLL keep the category-share drift_value/rebalance_quantity at the valuation's implied unit price; a row valued at 0 without its own SOLL has no share and carries both as null. With the position rows, computation_basis states the drift share's basis and lists the gaps where it is null. The 100% basis is securities + counting cash. An optional view (a view id) scopes the breakdown to that bucket view's holdings and is echoed. include_positions=false returns the category roll-up without the position rows, and min_drift (an absolute drift-weight threshold as a Decimal string, e.g. "0.02") returns only the category rows whose |drift_weight| meets it — targetless categories are filtered out with it, kept rows come back flat (an ancestor under the threshold is absent), and the response states positions_included, the applied min_drift and categories_total (the pre-filter count). tax_context=true attaches the current-year tax-free trim budgets (per holder, with their activity-aware staleness; holder-scoped, never portfolio-scoped). Raw position-target rows and per-category roll-up (the maintenance view): portfolixir.targets.list_positions.

min_drift.description: absolute drift-weight threshold as a finite, non-negative Decimal string, e.g. "0.02"; NaN or Infinity answers 422

tools.name: portfolixir.portfolios.category_results
tools.title: Per-category result (invested, value, made)
tools.description: What each category of a classification tree COST, what it is WORTH now, and what it has MADE (ADR-0041): invested (the members' base_cost, without the buys' fees and taxes), current_value, result_abs and result_pct per category, with the member positions behind it. Basis: the CURRENT COMPOSITION (the positions filed under each category today), no period, membership variant or as-of, NOT a time-weighted series (§6). result_pct is the sum of results over the sum of invested, NEVER a mean of the members' percentages. Priced as the valuation: latest quote, without one its last own trade price (ADR-0010; price_source (quote | trade) per position). A member whose result is not derivable (neither quote nor trade price, or no base-currency decomposition, ADR-0033) is excluded from BOTH sides of the sum, listed under excluded with its reason (excluded_members: once per tree, with native_costs), never as zero; covered_count and member_count state the coverage. Nothing invested: result_pct null, not "0". Parents roll up the same way. Realized results and income are NOT included (§5). Scope: portfolio_id in its base currency, a view narrowing within it; view alone: that view across EVERY portfolio, each account counted once, in EUR; neither: every portfolio, in EUR (a cost not paid in EUR is excluded as missing_base_cost); scope, view_id and base_currency state it. Decimal strings.

tools.name: portfolixir.portfolios.risk
tools.title: Portfolio risk/concentration lens
tools.description: Risk/concentration lens for a portfolio over the steerable basis (the valued positions, scoped by the active view): single-name Top-N (default 10, override top_n, capped at 1000; the answer echoes the applied top_n) with a severity (ok/warn/hard) per instrument type (stock warn>7/hard>10, ETF warn>25), the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (hhi) on the 0-10000 scale with a band (low<1500, moderate, concentrated>2500), and opt-in asset-class cap violations (asset_class_caps, e.g. {"equity":"50"}) returning only classes over cap with the overage in percentage points. Weights, caps and HHI are 0-100 percentage Decimal strings. An optional view (a view id) scopes the lens to that bucket view's holdings and is echoed. The response also carries metrics (ADR-0047, FR-40), the portfolio's or view's derived figures on this same read: volatility, max_drawdown (with peak_date, trough_date, recovery_date; all three null at a drawdown of exactly 0: no decline) and risk_adjusted_return over 30d/90d/365d, read from the TTWROR chain's flow-adjusted daily return factors — NEVER the day-over-day change of the value, so a deposit or a withdrawal is not a return and a saver reads the same risk as a holder. Volatility is the population standard deviation of daily returns annualized by the square root of 365 (the walk is a calendar walk). risk_adjusted_return is the annualized mean daily excess return over risk_free_rate (a Decimal fraction, default 0 — at 0 it is return per unit of risk, and the rate is never inferred or fetched) divided by the volatility; it is null when the volatility is exactly 0. A volatility, a risk_adjusted_return or a correlation pair whose square root lies outside the double range is null WITHOUT insufficient_data: undefined, not short of data, not a reason to retry. correlations is the Pearson matrix of at most the 20 leading names of the Top-N list (correlations.leading_names states how many; the matrix is bounded, the list is not), their daily returns converted to the base currency first and computed over the days BOTH securities closed on, each pair with its overlap count; a security whose currency has no stored rate path is listed in excluded instead. Every metric carries its window, its observations and required — the minimum it needs — in both states; below it the value is null with insufficient_data true at HTTP 200, a gap marker and not a reason to retry. metrics.computation_basis states the series, gaps and assumptions once. THIS READ REPORTS, IT DOES NOT EVALUATE: there is no signal, recommendation, rating, score or action in the payload.

top_n.description: Top-N length (default 10, at most 1000); the answer echoes the applied top_n

risk_free_rate.description: annual risk-free rate as a Decimal fraction (0.02 is 2 % p.a.) for risk_adjusted_return; default 0

tools.name: portfolixir.policy_rules.list
tools.title: Stored policy rules
tools.description: The stored policy rules for a portfolio (ADR-0049): caps, floors and bands on a figure the product serves — a weight, a drift, the HHI, the portfolio volatility or maximum drawdown — stored as objects, not prose in a prompt. READ THE RULES HERE, not from memory: the rule in force is the one stored. Use it when a raised or lowered line has left the name saying the old figure; retiring and re-creating the rule would split its history. A rule none of whose versions has ever been in force answers 409 — delete it instead. A version added while the retirement runs waits for it and never survives it; a rule deleted meanwhile answers 404. Journaled under the API token.

tools.title: Delete a rule nobody was measured against

tools.name: portfolixir.portfolios.policy_findings
tools.title: Did anything cross a line?
tools.description: The stored policy rules in force TODAY for one evaluation context (ADR-0049), evaluated at read over the figures the product already serves — one call instead of re-deriving them. One finding per rule, sorted breached, undetermined, ok: state breached (strictly beyond the line), ok, or undetermined — the figure could not be read (reason insufficient_data with the metric's required and observations, undefined, no_active_plan, no_target, empty_basis, unvalued, subject_not_found, not_measured), which is NEVER a pass and is never filtered out by default. Each finding carries the rule's words (rule_name, rule_name_author, subject, measure, kind, severity, note, author), the thresholds and the measured value as Decimal strings on the measure's scale, the signed distance to the nearest line, and its computation_basis naming the read it used; the payload carries summary (counts per state) and computation_basis. status narrows (status=breached is the retrievable alarm list); view selects the context. PULL ONLY: nothing is pushed anywhere. A finding is a stored rule applied to a figure and carries no action — it neither proposes nor sizes a trade. A Portfolio Performance re-import does not destroy the policy rules: re-applying an export, the same one or a later one with renamed or re-ISINed securities, leaves every rule and every version in place with the same ids and the same subjects — securities survive a re-import, and categories and views are Portfolixir's own. A security, category, classification or view a rule reads cannot be deleted: the delete answers 409 naming the rules.

view.description: the evaluation context: the rules of this view (default: the portfolio-wide rules)
